title: Fired for Dizzy, rehired after Body and Soul, then to Basie
summary: Millinder replaced him with Gillespie, then rehired him; Basie's book was mostly head arrangements.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: He had trouble with his teeth or something, you know. And he was a good trumpet player. He was a fantastic trumpet player, geemanetti, he could play. And when he took ill, Herschel -- we were all staying at the same rooming house, Herschel Evans, Jo Jones, Page said, why don't you get Harry, you know. And in fact, Lucky had fired me for Dizzy. He fired me for Dizzy Gillespie. And because --
Well, had you given him any trouble or --

No. Well, Charlie and Rama had played with Dizzy so they wanted somebody in the band that they had played with. You know, they were good buddies. And I'm from St. Louis, you know. But Dizzy and I got in a little -- we started playing some "Body and Soul" in a place in Philadelphia one night and I kind of made a little noise that night, playing "Body and Soul." So Lucky hired me back. And Dizzy went with Teddy Hill. Come the side 3 - end

But after we went from Philadelphia back to New York, that's when Bobby Moore took ill and I -- Herschel and Jo, they recommended me to Basie and I took his place, you know. And -- oh, that was the latter part of 1937. But I still wanted to learn more about music because when I joined Basie's band, it was nothing but head arrangements. Everything was head arrangements. They didn't have -- I bet they didn't have 10 manuscripts, you know.
